The one large positive in the baseline, 2026-07-01 at +8.53%, came from a 17% EPS beat plus a brand-new $3bn savings programme, not from a reaffirmation. And this particular reaffirmation was visibly SOLD: the stock went from $39.26 on 09-03 to $35.96 by 09-10. So the residual value of this finding is only the truncation of the left tail — the market sold it because it wanted a raise, not because it doubts the floor — and it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.why_not_priced: Partially priced and I say so. What is not in the price is the TIMING: the wire copy read 'reaffirms guidance at a conference', which the market treats as a mid-quarter statement, and the quarter had in fact already closed. If the market had read it as a post-close pre-announcement, the stock would not have de-rated a further 8% into the print and the front-expiry straddle would not be 1.8x this name's median realised reaction. The specific observable: an implied event move of 5.55% on a name whose guidance range was marked to the completed quarter a fortnight ago.
evidence.independence: Fiscal-period convention confirmed by the prior-year Q1 release covering the quarter ended 31 August 2025 (https://investors.generalmills.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/General-Mills-Reports-Fiscal-2026-First-quarter-Results-and-Reaffirms-Full-year-Outlook/default.aspx). The Q1 consumption detail beyond the press-release text comes from a second write-up of the same fireside chat (https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/general-mills-at-barclays-consumer-conference-growth-push-gains-traction-93CH-4456937), so that detail and finding 2 SHARE the 2026-09-08 event as a source and are two readings of one day.

evidence.text: At the same 2026-09-08 fireside chat management said input-cost inflation is tracking toward the HIGH END of the guided 4-5% range with hedge coverage only 6-9 months out (~9 months on crops), while on the 2026-07-01 call it had already said fiscal 2027 profit is weighted to the second half because 'the impact of inflation net of cost savings is expected to be negative in the first quarter' — so the quarter being reported is the one where cost leverage is worst and the $750m of FY2027 savings has not yet phased in.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This lands INSIDE what the company has already guided, which by construction makes it a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and GIS's own precedent for a bad-margin Q1 with the year reaffirmed is -0.77% (2025-09-17, gross margin 33.9%, down 90bp). The baseline's two largest down reactions, -5.11% (2025-06-25) and -3.06% (2024-12-18), were guidance events rather than pure Q1 margin events. Sized small for that reason.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-08 press release headline was 'reaffirms annual guidance'; the high-end-of-range inflation detail and the 6-9 month hedge window sat in the fireside chat and not in the release, so it travelled through transcript coverage rather than the wire. If it were fully in the price, the 30-day consensus drift would not have gone UP 1.4% (from $0.71 to $0.72) over exactly the window containing that statement. That said, it is inside a guided range, which is why it is sized below one point.
evidence.independence: The first-half cost-savings phasing is independently sourced to the 2026-07-01 earnings call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/01/general-mills-gis-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), a different document and a different date. This finding shares the 2026-09-08 event with finding 1; the two are opposite-signed readings of the same day and are deliberately not double-counted.

evidence.text: The option market is paying an event-implied 5.55% (7.75% front-expiry straddle, 38.3% ATM IV) with a +2.75 put skew on a name whose last seven prints have a median absolute reaction of 3.06% and a maximum of 8.53%, while the short base — 46.0m shares, 8.64% of float, 5.60 days to cover — is already covering from 49.1m, and the entire +8.53% reaction to the 2026-07-01 print has been given back (spot $35.805 against a $40.08 director-grant price on 2026-08-30).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the baseline's seven reactions were negative, but six of seven were inside 5.55% and five of seven were inside 3.5%. The one time this name exceeded the currently-implied move was 2026-07-01, which required a 17% EPS beat plus a new multi-year savings programme. Nothing of that class is on the table on 2026-09-23.
evidence.why_not_priced: I am signing against the skew, so I have to say why the option market is wrong about THIS print: the downside being bought is dividend-cut and structural-derating contagion — Campbell's cut its dividend 36% on 2026-09-03 and GIS fell 3.25% the same day, and GIS now yields ~6.8% — but a dividend cut is not an event this print can deliver. GIS declared its $0.61 quarterly dividend with the 2026-07-01 release (paid 2026-08-03) and the next board declaration sits with the late-September annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, outside the window. If the skew were about the quarter rather than about the payout and the sector, the put/call open-interest ratio would not be 0.55. The counterweight is real and is why this is [sizing note removed].7 rather than 2: the resolved record has a hunter losing 11 points to a large put skew, and a covering short base is a reason to shrink a negative, not a licence to enlarge a positive.
evidence.independence: The Campbell's dividend cut and the same-day GIS move are sourced separately (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/03/campbells-slides-9-36-dividend-cut-general-mills-falls-4-kraft-heinz-drops-3/, 2026-09-03). The implied-move and skew numbers come from the sealed baseline, not from this URL. Cutting the other way, and recorded rather than buried: the 2026-09-08 reaffirmation was met with an ~8% five-session decline (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Why+General+Mills+(GIS)+Stock+Is+Down+Today, 2026-09-10), which is evidence the marginal holder is selling regardless of the guide.

evidence.text: General Mills is a PLAINTIFF, with Mars, Kellanova and McKee Foods, in an antitrust suit filed 2026-09-04 in federal court in Chicago alleging US sugar producers fixed granulated sugar prices from January 2017 to at least October 2024 — a gain contingency, not a liability, that no preview treats as an asset and that cannot resolve on 2026-09-23.

The Brazil business (Yoki, Kitano) was sold to 3coracoes for a R$800m base price and CLOSED on 2026-09-03, which is fiscal Q2 2027 and not the quarter being reported; the $1,032m non-cash pre-tax held-for-sale valuation loss was already taken in Q4 FY2026, so any final close adjustment and CTA recycling lands in the December print.

The next quarterly dividend declaration falls with the late-September board/annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, payable 2026-11-03 — so the payout question the 6.8% yield is pricing is not settled by this print.

A Pet/Blue Buffalo negative worth filing: GIS's own 2026-09-08 line that Blue Buffalo Wilderness 'may take 18 months to 2 years to return to growth' plus the guided low-single-digit FY27 retail-inventory headwind is pre-guided, Pet is only ~14% of sales ($610m of $4.52bn in the year-ago quarter) against a North America Retail segment management says gained share in 8 of its top 10 categories, and the independent read cuts the other way — Chewy on 2026-09-09 said the pet market 'did not meaningfully recover... but also did not deteriorate further' and RAISED its FY outlook (https://investor.chewy.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Chewy-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). Net of the rest of the company this is not a finding, so it is not one.

A 'low bar on seasonality' argument: $0.72 is 23.2% of the $3.10 FY27 midpoint against $0.86 / ~$3.60 = 23.9% for the prior year. The bar is normal for a GIS Q1, not conspicuously low, so I dropped this line rather than sizing it.

Insider signal: all Form 4s since 2026-06-01 are routine — non-employee director retainer shares issued 2026-05-31 at $33.65 and 2026-08-30 at $40.08 under the 2022 Stock Compensation Plan (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040704/000162828026059544/wk-form4_1788200689.xml). No open-market cluster.

A causal, company-specific explanation for the -12.5% 20-day run-up beyond sector de-rating, the Campbell's dividend cut on 09-03, a JPMorgan Sell reiteration and an Evercore target trim to $38 on 09-14: there isn't one, and an unexplained drawdown on a 17-analyst mega-cap is not evidence of over-reaction.

The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management [sizing note removed]. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the reconciliation of a consensus print against the company's own quarterly guide, and the inconsistency is visible only as an internal contradiction in the estimate set (EPS on guidance, revenue below it). If it were priced, previews would be flagging a 'low bar on revenue' rather than quoting the $9.47bn as the bar; instead Zacks' preview quotes it straight. I keep the size small and let the band cross zero because the marginal holder of a mega-cap trades the buy-side bar, not the Zacks bar, and MDT has twice in the last four prints sold off on a headline beat.

evidence.text: As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is an absence, and absences do not generate wire copy — there is no article saying 'Medtronic has not yet filed the exchange-offer S-4'. If the market had priced a slip, previews would be discussing whether FY27 guidance gets re-based rather than repeating the June 'full twelve months of Diabetes' framing. The band crosses zero because the standard sequencing is to launch an exchange offer immediately after a quarterly release, so the same fact can flip to a positive on 1 September.
evidence.independence: Cross-checked against Medtronic's own EDGAR index (no 8-K since 2026-06-03, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001613103&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=60) and against the 2026-08-17 DEF 14A, whose only capital resolution is the routine annual 'overseas market purchases' authority, with no off-market purchase or exchange-offer resolution for the 15 October AGM.

evidence.text: The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).
evidence.why_not_priced: A missed soft deadline on an event with no announced date produces no headline and no estimate revision, so there is nothing for the tape to have reflected. If it were priced you would see notes handicapping the margin target, as happened around every peer's activist-driven capital markets day. The 1 September call is the natural venue to set a date, so the sign is genuinely two-sided and the band is wide.
evidence.independence: Independent of the other findings. Corroborated only by absence: the Medtronic newsroom listing through 2026-08-20 (https://news.medtronic.com/) contains no Investor Day announcement.

evidence.text: Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I am sizing it accordingly. MDT rose 3.2% on 27-28 July, i.e. before the BSX print, and only 0.8% on 29 July itself, so the tape does not look like it repriced Medtronic's CAS line on the read-across. But the 80%-penetration remark is the bearish half of the same disclosure and cuts the other way, which is exactly why a single number here is not worth more than a few tenths.
evidence.independence: Overlaps with nothing else I found; the Affera CE Mark expansion for ventricular arrhythmias on 2026-08-06 (https://news.medtronic.com/) points the same way on the franchise but is a European label, not a US volume datapoint.

evidence.text: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Edge series is published in jewelry trade press (JCK, InStore, Edge's own blog) five days before the print and is not carried by any financial wire, terminal or aggregator; Signet has only ~3 EPS estimates on the tape, so there is no sell-side machine converting a trade-press monthly into a Q3 comp. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -13.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and Citi would not have opened a public 'upside 30-day catalyst watch' on 2026-09-08 expecting a raise to the top end of the range. The same series was benign through the quarter itself (+12/+18/+10 in May/Jun/Jul), so this is specifically a forward-guide signal, not a restatement of the Q2 print. Note the level is not transferable — Edge ran +12% in April while Signet comped +1.8% in Q1 — the sequential shape is the signal, and it is a ~7pt one-month deceleration.
evidence.independence: Two different sources point the same way on the value-end consumer: PROG Holdings' Q2 2026 call named jewelry as one of only two categories at Purchasing Power that failed to grow GMV year over year (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/prog-prg-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), and Pandora's calendar-Q2 2026 report showed North America like-for-like negative with US sales only 'stable' (https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/pandora-q2-results-2026-guidance-raised-early-announcement-1239092531/). The May/June/July Edge readings come from the same source cluster as this finding and are deliberately folded into it rather than filed separately.

evidence.text: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro trade-law event that lands in the index, not in SIG's relative price; converting it requires knowing the specific sentence in Signet's 2026-06-02 call ('mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year') and that the guide was built on the 15% Section 122 number. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
evidence.independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. This finding and the refund finding below share the tariff theme but rest on different documents (a USTR action versus Signet's own disclosure); they should be collapsed to one residual if scored as a cluster.

evidence.text: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: The item is knowably excluded from guidance by the company's own words, and it is unquantifiable from outside — which is exactly why no estimate carries it and why the wire preview cannot contain it. The 'how any proceeds may be used' phrasing is a buyback tell: Signet has $355m remaining on the 2017 authorisation after a $50m ASR on 2026-06-08 and had $602.8m cash / ~$1.7bn liquidity at Q1, against a $3.2bn market cap. If the market were carrying this, the stock would not be at 8x the midpoint of a $9.20–$11.00 FY27 EPS guide and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 3.27. Wide band because the refund may land as a Q3 event, be excluded from adjusted EPS, or be deferred into contested CIT proceedings.
evidence.independence: The refund mechanism and its timing come from a different source entirely — Skadden's account of the post-Supreme-Court CBP refund process (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape) — and the buyback capacity from Signet's 2026-06-08 8-K item 8.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832988/000083298826000161/sig-20260608.htm). evidence.why_not_priced: This is guidance arithmetic across two press releases and a transcript, and only 8 analysts cover the name — stockanalysis.com records that their price targets were last updated 2026-06-04, when CXM closed at $5.38, with one refresh since. If the H2 bar were in the price, the average target would not still sit at $7.88 below a $7.99 spot with the stock at a 12-month high; the sell-side has simply not re-underwritten the FY27 OI ramp since the guide was cut, so a second cut lands into unrevised models rather than into pre-positioned ones.

evidence.text: The Q2 FY27 revenue guide implies professional services of only ~$20.5m (total $214-215m less subscription $193.5-194.5m) versus actual PS of $24.7m, $27.2m and $28.8m in the last three quarters, and Sprinklr beat its own implied PS guide by 25% in Q3 FY26 ($28.8m actual vs $23.0m implied) and 10% in Q1 FY27 ($24.7m vs $22.5m implied) — so a headline revenue beat of roughly 1.5-2.5% is mechanically likely, but at the -10% PS gross margin management guided it adds nothing to operating income.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire carries 'Sprinklr poised to beat earnings estimates again' as an undifferentiated positive; what it does not carry is that the beat is structurally located in the one revenue line that runs a negative gross margin, so the headline and the margin move in opposite directions. If this were priced, the sell-side would model PS separately and the stock would not react to the total-revenue line — yet the 2026-06-03 print beat revenue, EPS and operating income and still closed down 3%, which is exactly what a market reading the total line and then the guide does.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q1 FY27 transcript with finding 2, so treat as one source cluster on the guidance-quality point; the PS actuals are from three separate press releases (Q3 FY26 https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251203552368/en/Sprinklr-Announces-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Results, Q4 FY26 https://investors.sprinklr.com/news/press-releases/detail/249/sprinklr-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026, Q1 FY27 https://www.sprinklr.com/newsroom/sprinklr-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results/).

evidence.why_not_priced: This table is in a 6MB 10-Q note; it is not in the earnings press release, it was not raised on the Q1 call, and no wire copy on the name mentions it. If the market had focused on a declining US base at ~51% of revenue, the story on the tape would be 'domestic decline offset by emerging-market wins', not 'AI transformation and improving renewals' — and a stock whose largest region shrinks does not close at a 12-month high on a 22.6% 20-day run without one analyst refreshing a target since 2026-06-04.

evidence.why_not_priced: Management framed this on the Q1 call as a discrete quarter event — 54 customers 'moved on the fly' out of a damaged Middle East environment to Ireland and '$3 million to $4 million of slip deals' — and the market treated it as behind them: CXM bottomed at $4.91 on 2026-06-25 and then rose 67% with no company news. If the market had carried it forward into Q2 it would not have re-rated the stock 67% while the same conflict was still striking Gulf data centres in July, and the unquantified infrastructure and remediation costs would show up in sell-side gross-margin estimates that have not been revised since 2026-06-04.

evidence.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing the germanium input, LPTH would have decoupled from the drone complex during the August unwind. It did not: on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-28 LPTH fell alongside Ondas, Unusual Machines, Red Cat and Kratos - names with zero germanium exposure and opposite YTD performance - which is the signature of positioning, not of anyone re-underwriting LightPath's input economics. A market that had priced this would show LPTH's 20-day beta to the c-UAS basket breaking down and 25-delta skew tilted to calls; instead skew is +1.21 vol points (mildly put-bid) and the stock tracked the basket point for point. Ge substitution is also the specific mechanism management named as the order driver on 2025-09-25, so the call has a live, quantifiable hook the tape is ignoring.

evidence.text: An April 16, 2026 side letter fixed the G5 Infrared Year-2 earnout at exactly $9.0M ($6.3M cash + $2.7M stock, payable 1-15 January 2027) against a carried liability of only $6.7M at 31 March 2026 - so roughly $2.3M of additional non-cash fair-value/accretion charge is arithmetically locked into the Q4 FY26 P&L, on top of the $1.78M Amorphous Materials earnout accrual, guaranteeing a GAAP loss materially wider than the single published ($0.02) estimate and a $6.3M cash outflow four months out.
evidence.why_not_priced: With a single published EPS estimate on the name and no sell-side model visible that reconciles the side letter, the headline GAAP number that hits the wires and the algos at 16:05 ET is pre-determined to look like a large miss versus ($0.02). If this were priced there would be a visible adjusted-vs-GAAP bridge in the previews and the estimate itself would sit nearer ($0.06)-($0.09); instead the aggregators still carry ($0.02). The offset - and why I size this small rather than large - is that this base has looked through identical earnout noise before: the 11-Feb-2026 print carried a fair-value charge and the stock rose 21.5%.
evidence.independence: Independent read of the same side letter by a buy-side writer, published 2026-05-13, noting the Year-2 earnout was locked at the $9M maximum and that the earnout was creating $3.4M of non-cash charges and $3.8M of operating cash impact per quarter: https://cupofcoffeecapital.substack.com/p/lightpath-q3-2026-breakdown . evidence.text: Buried in the body of the 22 July 2026 8-K on the China divestiture - not in the press release and not in any wire story - is a five-year supply-back obligation under which the divested Zhenjiang plant sells product to LightPath at cost plus a markup that starts at 10% and steps up 5 points for every $1M of the $4.5M purchase price the buyer repays, capped at cost plus 30%, so LightPath's own input cost rises mechanically as it collects its sale proceeds.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every wire item on this deal reported the same three facts - $4.5M price, five-year installments, management buyer, 'fully Western-aligned footprint' - and none reported the markup escalator. The press release exhibit itself discloses only that China contributed ~$4.5M of third-party revenue and is silent on cost of goods. Zhenjiang was the in-house low-cost molded-optics plant supplying the Visible Components line at internal cost; converting that to cost+10% rising to cost+30% is a structural gross-margin headwind against management's stated 40% target, which they were already guiding as slipping 'a quarter or 2'. If the market had read the agreement, the 40% margin bridge would be being questioned in previews; it is not being mentioned at all.
evidence.independence: Corroborating on the other side of the same transaction, the 23 July 2026 press release quantifies only the revenue that leaves ($4.5M/yr of third-party sales) and says nothing about cost: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/889971/000143774926024234/ex_991571.htm .
